negative_sampling_rule_from_code.build_candidate_frame_L149_151: cand = (~active) & (dist_m <= buffer_m); if require_burnable: cand = cand & (static.burnable_frac > 0.05)
negative_sampling_rule_from_code.buffer_m: 6000.0 (fixed; run_routing_integration.py:106 build_dataset(..., buffer_m=6000.0), unchanged across both runs)
negative_sampling_rule_from_code.label_L217: newly = nxt.cumulative_mask & ~active  # positives = ignite by next overpass
negative_sampling_rule_from_code.key_property: Negatives are ALL burnable, not-yet-active cells within the SAME fixed 6 km buffer of the CURRENT active footprint that do NOT ignite by the next overpass. There is NO random negative subsampling and NO distance-conditioned negative selection: positives and negatives are drawn from an identical, distance-symmetric candidate set. The hypothesised mechanism ('samples negatives farther from the fire') has no code path.
